newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW Australia removes apple ban on other states.
newsitem.headline: NSW Australia removes apple ban on other states.

text.p: The Australian state of New South Wales would recommence interstate trade in apples and pears from Victoria and South Australia, state Agriculture Minister Richard Amery said in a statement.
Trade in the fruit and in certain nursery stock from Victoria and South Australia was restricted while tests were conducted in Germany to determine the presence of the bacterial disease fire blight.
"Unfortunately, the German tests on cotoneaster plants from the Melbourne Botanic Gardens have proved positive to fire blight," he said on Friday.
"Further testing of plant material from the Adelaide Botanic Gardens has also shown some positive reaction to the disease," he said.
"A concerted effort is being made by agricultural authorities and industry to eradicate the existing, minor infection," he said.
A scientific and industry consultative committee had established a 15 km quarantine zone around the sites, he said.
Fire blight could seriously reduce production from commercial orchards but the disease did not affect the quality of the fruit, he said.
Signed area freedom certificates would have to be produced to allow restrictions placed on apples and pears from the two states to be lifted, he said.
Nursery stock must be certified free of fire blight by regulatory authorities before movement would be permitted, he said.
Australia's Federal Minister for Primary Industries John Anderson announced on Thursday that surveys had failed to detect fire blight in commercial orchards around Australia.
However, fire blight had been found to be present on a limited number of ornamental host plants in the botanical gardens in Melbourne Victoria, and in Adelaide, South Australia, he said.
Laboratory tests in Victoria had officially cleared the state's major apple and pear growing regions of fire blight, the Australian Apple and Pear Growers Association said on Monday.
